target.name: Zipline
target.founder: Keller Rinaudo Cliffton, Keenan Wyrobek, Will Hetzler

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $8.6B.

data.narrative:
Zipline, a Series H autonomous delivery platform, is valued at $7.6B after raising $1.63B to date. The valuation is assessed against a universe of four same-sector peers in Drones & Autonomous spanning both private and public stages: Wayve ($8.6B, Series D), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), Nuro ($6.0B, Series G), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B, public).

Peer-median valuation is the primary applicable triangulation method, yielding $6.4B across the four comparables. This method reflects the observable range of $3.3B to $8.6B within the peer set and anchors to companies at similar development and funding stages. The median approach avoids distortion from outliers while capturing sector-wide valuation patterns for autonomous delivery and mobility platforms.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5B to $7.4B, with a median of $6.4B. Zipline's current $7.6B valuation sits above this range, implying a 18% premium to peer median. Key uncertainties include the limited comp universe (n=4) and heterogeneity in peer stage progression—ranging from Series D to public—which may not fully capture Zipline's specific operational maturity, unit economics, or market position within autonomous last-mile delivery. Additional data on revenue multiples or deployment scale would strengthen conviction.
